explanation: The recorded descent was progressing and ended with lease_exhausted, not stalled. Its 4.39 mm pose residual was incorrectly compared with a fixed 4 mm cutoff rather than the rim-contact band. At the supplied state, the own-geometry common vertical half-band is approximately 7.50 mm, the pad-to-planned-rim height difference approximately 4.22 mm, and the saved rim-height uncertainty 2.44 mm: the old cutoff alone does not establish failed insertion. The repair first obtains current local evidence and evaluates actual componentwise overlap, without resetting, reopening, discarding the saved tracker, or automatically repeating descent. It permits a locally supported nominal closure trial with independent retention testing when conservative margins are inconclusive. If correction is needed, its bounded lease covers the remaining distance; stalls are inspected without another push. All later grasp, transfer, release and final-assessment logic is retained.
interface:
Entry: main(api), returning completion_proposed and JSON-compatible evidence. A proposal is not official success. This is one source replacement in the insertion phase; the remaining method and Jev definitions are preserved.

Observation dependencies and gates:
1. Initial shape/support: same-body identity, upright circular widest rim, original support, destination support plane and footprint. Witnesses are measured lip surfaces plus calibrated visible-boundary rays, separate source/deck/burner surface samples, and visible deck corners. Geometry uses geo.plane coefficients, geo.circle_xy and api.plane_point. Failed named measurements are checked through membership and measurement_errors and replaced by another view/arc. Radius and supported height become rigid shape invariants, not live detections. Neither a surface sample nor an inferred hidden corner is treated as an object center.
2. Approach: only current partial source-rim agreement, open-finger entry geometry and a candidate local pinch are needed. Numerical candidates use geo.rotation, the actual opening axis, pad offset, pad extents and finger bounds. A consistent short-horizon world-circle prior is retained with uncertainty; a camera change alone does not invalidate it. Possible interaction, changed support, incompatible partial measurements or unknown identity requires remeasurement or stops the affected action. No later route certificate is required.
3. Repaired insertion: first inspect the current physical state with jaws open. Current g0/g1 may be any obtainable rim lip portions; they are local geometric samples, not old corner correspondences. A review separately reports identity, stationary-prior consistency, visible straddle/prospective entry alignment/partial consistency, external obstruction, visibility and support for a bounded trial. At least one compatible current lip sample and consistent source evidence can support the short-horizon circle prior. Missing or inconsistent samples trigger a fresh update of the saved patch and its independently measured envelope binding; inadequate registration falls back to current rim-arc measurements from alternative surfaces/views. New geometry must remain consistent with source support; observed changes do not silently authorize a lateral regrasp. If the new measurement resolves a previously missing dependency, a bounded updated review can reconsider local authorization rather than retaining an obsolete unknown decision.
   Actual pad_center comes from geo.pad_position, not the TCP. The common vertical band is derived from the actual tool rotation and supplied pad extents, reducing it for tilt across the pad envelope. Tangential overlap uses the actual tool-frame residual. Vertical and tangential nominal overlaps and uncertainty-reduced margins are separate; own finger bounds also give the local support gap. These are geometric trial predicates, not proof of contact. Positive nominal overlap plus current entry/straddle evidence and supported_local_trial permits closure followed by the existing independent retention test; negative conservative margins are reported as uncertainty, not impossibility. No future controller allowance is charged as an unobserved current displacement.
   If overlap is absent, at most two additional correction leases are allowed, each sized from remaining distance (4..24 calls). Fresh local observations follow motion even if the lease reports reached. Exhaustion with progress is not called a stall; a stalled lease can be inspected but cannot authorize another push. Persisted correction intent/count, current partial measurements and receipt/effect evidence survive repair. A new source revision never undoes motion. Budget exhaustion or unsupported local action stops with the exact gap.
4. Retention: requires current same-body rigid-patch or uniquely corresponding landmark measurements before and after a locally justified lift, plus actual robot states. geo.attachment_error and measured patch progress are compared with hand motion; neither closure nor a track alone proves grasping. Existing tracker handles are reused only with fresh quality checks. Unknown registration requests the saved physical landmark definitions when available; ambiguous correspondence is rejected separately from body identity. A different identified patch can initialize a new prospective test without registering to old rim landmarks. At most three retention tests; no reopening during transfer.
5. Envelope/route: only transported center, lower extent, radius, tilt and their relevant component bounds are needed. Patch-to-envelope propagation needs adequate rotational observability; otherwise current rim-arc geometry binds a new envelope. Local translation evidence does not itself establish a full pose. Only the next bounded hand/bowl leg is reviewed. External obstruction, no observed obstruction, robot/bowl occlusion and unobserved space have distinct meanings. Missing blocker measurements receive a replacement request; a measured blocker top can motivate a separately reviewed upward leg. Self-occlusion is not an obstacle, and missing visibility is not certified clearance. Unsupported motion stops; justified partial-visibility progress uses shorter legs. Stalls preserve the jaws.
6. Lower/release: current horizontal containment and bottom/support gap are separate predicates. Retained radius/height, current registered or remeasured geometry, and current support review supply the witnesses. Nominal and uncertainty-reduced margins are reported separately. Lowering is followed by an actual relation review; a stall is not repeatedly pushed. A supported small-drop trial is bounded by the measured gap uncertainty. Unknown registration can use corresponding landmarks or a new patch plus current rim geometry. Jaw transition intent and acknowledgment are checkpointed before later observations can fail.
7. Final: after opening and retreat, two fresh observations must show the same upright bowl on the stove support with bounded world-position drift, support-height consistency and footprint containment, separated by at least six physical steps. A camera/view change is not object motion. Missing post-release evidence leads to bounded additional observation or an incomplete result, never automatic regrasp.

Persistence: bowl_v2 retains measured invariants and provenance, phase intent, acknowledged jaw transitions, useful tracker handle/camera/ROI/reference identity, semantic landmark definitions, envelope binding and pending absolute targets. Historical references are not current detections. The insertion additions are bounded to two lip samples, one compact effect record, counters and the existing eight-entry diagnostic window; no dense clouds or nested checkpoint histories are stored. Uncertainty estimates and local rigid/planar/circular models are heuristic, not calibrated certificates. Fixture priors are invalidated by observed displacement, relevant contact or inconsistent current geometry. All review calls have exact structured fields; schema adherence is not evidence truth. All numerical helper fields and API paths in this replacement were checked against the supplied manual.
jev_protocol:
All motion remains api.control, directly for jaw transitions or through bounded api.drive leases. The existing questions have exactly x,y,z,rx,ry,rz,gripper. Each axis question names its world axis and uses its host-bound goal_relation: negative=decrease, hold=within_tolerance, positive=increase. Gripper choices are exactly open, close, keep according to objective.gripper. Answers are dispatched unchanged; quaternions are xyzw and rotation errors are world rotation vectors.

Python computes pad targets, opening axis, common vertical band, tangential residual, support gap, uncertainty margins, tolerances and lease size. Jev receives the existing phase, target_pad_world, measured geometry, latest authorization/evidence and effect_not_certified features, together with trusted host robot state and signed residuals. It chooses semantic directions, not geometry or hidden contact state. Insertion now stores the actual overlap evidence before closing or correcting. Normal leases preserve orientation, use pad_center, limits of 0.02 m and 0.05 rad, three native steps and documented tolerances. The insertion lease is 4..24 calls, at most two corrections; ordinary phase leases remain unchanged. Jaw calls use measured pose, 0.001 m/0.01 rad limits and bounded delivery attempts.

Reached, moved, stalled and lease_exhausted are controller outcomes only. A progressing exhausted insertion can satisfy a separately observed overlap gate; a stalled insertion is not pushed again. Closure still requires independent object/hand differential motion before retention is claimed. Reviews, not Jev choices, provide current image interpretation and named RGB-D witnesses. The new insertion review declares body, prior, alignment, external, visibility and trial with explicit enums, including unknown where needed. It distinguishes a supported local trial from certified clearance and actual contact; all unmeasured outcomes remain limitations.
